stem.en: Malaria is eliminated from a region. Kabir says "so the sickle allele will disappear in a generation or two". What does the sim show?

text.en: It falls, slowly. Carriers are no longer protected, and two-copy children still die, but the allele is hidden in carriers and only exposed one child in four when two carriers meet. Over many generations it dwindles; it does not vanish quickly.
It disappears in a generation or two.

feedback.en: Selection removes it only through two-copy children, who are a small fraction. Hidden alleles fade slowly.

text.en: It stays exactly where it is.

feedback.en: Without the carrier advantage, the two-copy deaths tip the balance downward, and the frequency falls.

text.en: It rises, because carriers are now healthy.

feedback.en: Carriers were always healthy. What they lose is an advantage over non-carriers, and without it the allele has only its cost.

explanation.en: A recessive allele hides in carriers, so selection against it is weak when it is rare. Removing the benefit starts a slow decline, not a collapse.
